references.text: God's assessment of the animals as good, the final link in the repeated formula 'it was good' that culminates in v31 with 'very good'.
The psalmist praises God's diverse creation made with wisdom, reflecting God's own assessment of all He had done as 'very good'.
Thanks to God who created the heavens with wisdom and spread out the earth over the waters – an expression of the goodness of creation corresponding to God's satisfaction in Gen 1:31.
Let everything praise the Lord, for He commanded and it was created. The song of praise from creation reflects the goodness of creation confirmed in Gen 1:31.
'He has made everything beautiful in its time' – a reflection on the goodness of creation corresponding to God's assessment in Gen 1:31.
Creation reveals God's invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature – this presupposes the goodness of creation confirmed in Gen 1:31.
'Everything God has created is good' – a direct theological parallel to God's assessment of all creation as 'very good' in Gen 1:31.
The completion of the sixth day ('exceedingly good') is the direct prerequisite for the rest on the seventh day.
The local 'good' in the creative process culminates in the global 'exceedingly good' at its completion.
The sanctification of the Sabbath is a direct consequence of the creation work being finished and 'exceedingly good'.
The New Testament confirms that God's rest on the seventh day is a direct result of the completion of creation.
Moses' assessment of the completion of the tabernacle reflects God's assessment of the completion of creation.
The Sabbath commandment is directly grounded in the six days of creation and God's rest after its completion.
Repeated basis for the Sabbath based on the six days of creation and God's rest.
